metadata.title: Irreducibility of exposed-point varieties of discotopes
metadata.description:
This research note proves that the complex Zariski closure of the exposed points of every finite Minkowski sum of ellipsoidal discs of dimension at least two is irreducible, without genericity or full-dimensionality assumptions. It proves the exposed-point conjecture stated by Meroni in the 2023 Oberwolfach report. Under an explicit generic condition on summand spans, it also proves equality with the purely nonlinear part of Gesmundo and Meroni, resolving their 2022 irreducibility conjecture. A nongeneric example distinguishes the two varieties.

The proof combines a connected real-analytic support-point parametrization with a standard analytic irreducibility lemma. Earlier partial discotope results and the analytic precursor are credited. Historical first priority is not asserted. The source-and-verification archive includes the manuscript source, pinned exact checks, provenance, a dated priority audit, and independent adversarial reviews. Finite symbolic checks corroborate formulas and examples; they do not replace the universal proofs.

Generative AI tools were used extensively in proof development, literature triage, manuscript preparation, adversarial review, and symbolic-check design. This is an unrefereed preprint; no human peer review or formal proof certification is claimed. Research prose is licensed CC BY 4.0 and verification code is licensed MIT.
